# Moodle CLI 0.11.0

This release lets a student work in Moodle from the terminal day to day. You can read and send messages, reply and post in forums, submit online text, see the full calendar and see how much time a quiz has left. It also fixes three bugs that hid deadlines or grades, and the CLI now works when Moodle is installed under a subpath such as `https://host/moodle`.

## Highlights

- **Messages.** List, read and send direct and group messages, and mark them read.
- **Forum writes.** Reply to a post, start a discussion, attach files, and subscribe or unsubscribe.
- **Online-text submissions.** `submit --text` or `--text-file`, on its own or alongside files.
- **Calendar.** Course, user and site events, not just deadlines, with an `.ics` export.
- **Quiz timer.** Timed attempts show the time left and when the attempt ends.
- **Overdue work and every grade.** Overdue items you can still submit now appear in `due` and `todo`, and `grades` includes manual items and category totals.
- **Moodle under a subpath.** Paste any page address and the CLI finds the install root.

## Messages

```bash
moodle messages list
moodle messages show CONVERSATION
moodle messages send CONVERSATION "On my way"
moodle messages read --all
```

`alerts` now shows notification bodies and links as well as their subjects. The remote MCP server gains read tools for conversations and the calendar. Sending a message stays CLI-only.

## Forums

```bash
moodle threads reply POST "Thanks, that fixed it" --attach notes.pdf
moodle forums post FORUM --subject "Week 3 question" --text "..."
moodle forums subscribe FORUM
```

Each write is confirmed against the discussion page, so a reply that Moodle accepted is never posted twice. Too many attachments are refused before anything is uploaded. `threads show` now lists attachments with their name, size and URL, and forum ids are course-module ids everywhere.

## Submissions

```bash
moodle submit UNIT "Reflection" --text-file reflection.md
moodle submit UNIT "Report" report.pdf --text "Notes for the marker" --final
moodle submission show UNIT "Report"
moodle submission remove UNIT "Report"
```

Blank lines in the text are kept as paragraphs. If a submission includes both files and text, the confirmation prompt names both. `activities show` on an assignment now reports its description, your submitted text, files and comments, and the extension date, kept apart from feedback.

The first save of a submission can still stop with a message. A student session cannot tell whether a draft-only save would stay a draft or go straight to grading. Rather than guess, the CLI refuses that first save and suggests `--final` or saving in the browser. A `--final` first submission, saving over an existing draft and finalising a draft all work. If the site shows its submission statement only after a save, the CLI returns the saved receipt and the exact command to run again.

## Calendar

```bash
moodle calendar --days 30
moodle calendar --unit UNIT
moodle calendar --ics -o moodle.ics
```

Times use your Moodle profile time zone, not the machine's. Calendar events also appear in `overview`.

## Quizzes

`quiz show` and `quiz answer` report `time_left_s` and `ends_at`. When the page shows only a countdown, `ends_at` is worked out from the server clock and can be up to two seconds off. Formulas questions with several inputs can be answered with repeated `--value` flags, and each field shows its label (thanks @Neutralmilkzzz). A password-protected quiz resumed in a new session asks for the password again instead of failing.

## Activities

- `complete REF` marks an activity complete, and lists show completion state.
- A restricted activity reports `available: false` with the reason and exits 0.
- `activities show` on a label lists its embedded videos, and `activities captions LABEL --to FILE` saves their captions as SRT or VTT.
- `download` keeps folder subpaths instead of flattening them into `name (2).ext`.
- `open` prints the URL when there is no browser to open it, and respects `--dry-run`.

## Sites under a subpath

Moodle can live at `https://host/moodle` or deeper, and the CLI used to work only at the domain root. It now asks Moodle where its root is, starting from whatever address you paste: front page, dashboard, a course or the login page. It also follows a bare host's redirects through login directories, SSO providers and meta refreshes. `moodle auth site [address]` shows or sets the site. A saved address that points at a page is corrected the first time a command fails, and a wrong `MOODLE_BASE_URL` gets an exact fix hint. Thanks @autowert66 for finding the problem and the first fix.

## Fixes

- Dates on Chinese and Japanese sites are read correctly, including month and day suffixes.
- Announcement attachments appear in human output.
- The forum subscription session key is no longer placed in request URLs.
- The Moodle session is sent only to caption tracks hosted on the same Moodle install.
- Lockfile refresh for the `sharp` and `source-map-js` advisories.

## Validation

Every feature was checked against a disposable Moodle 5.0 lab with seeded students, groups, forums, quizzes and calendar events. All six theme, language and disabled-service variants passed, along with 16 acceptance checks. The one recorded limit is the first draft-only save described above. Details are in `docs/reviews/v0.11/`.
